title: Weak object pronouns: position, order, doubling

blocks.title: Where weak pronouns go
blocks.text:
Weak object pronouns have no stress of their own and lean on the verb. Their position is fixed by the form of the verb, not by style:

**Before** every finite verb, and after the particles θα, να, ας, δεν, μη(ν): **Το ξέρω. Θα σου το πω. Πρέπει να τον δεις. Ας το αφήσουμε. Δεν τη βρήκα. Μην το πεις.** The order is always particles → pronouns → verb. In the perfect tenses the pronoun goes before the auxiliary: **Το έχω δει.**

**After** a positive imperative and after a gerund: **Πες μου. Φέρ' το. Κοίταξέ με. Ρωτώντας τον…** Negative commands are not imperatives (they are μη + dependent), so the pronoun goes back in front: **Μην το αγγίξεις!**

Nothing may come between a weak pronoun and its verb: *Το ήδη είδα is impossible; say **Το είδα ήδη**. Two weak pronouns stand together, the **genitive** (indirect object) before the **accusative** (direct object): **Μου το έδωσε**, **Σου τα είπα**, **Τους το εξήγησα**.

blocks.title: Stress and elision after imperatives
blocks.text:
An imperative and its pronouns are pronounced as one word, and a Greek word cannot be stressed further back than the third syllable from the end. When the pronouns push the stress past that limit, a **second accent** is written:

• imperative stressed on the third syllable from the end + one pronoun: the accent goes on its last syllable: **κοίταξέ με, διάβασέ το, ετοίμασέ τα**.

• imperative stressed on the second syllable from the end + two pronouns: the first pronoun takes the accent: **δώσε μού το, φέρε μού τα, πάρε μού το**. With one pronoun no extra accent is needed: **φέρε το, δώσε μου**.

• before a finite verb a pronoun is never stressed, but a *distinguishing* accent is written where it could be misread as a possessive: **Η μυρωδιά μού θυμίζει…** 'the smell reminds me…' vs **η μυρωδιά μου** 'my smell'.

• three-syllable imperative + two pronouns: the extra accent goes on the imperative: **διάβασέ μου το**. The gerund behaves the same way: **δίνοντάς του το**.

In speech the final -ε of a short imperative usually drops before a pronoun, which solves the stress problem: **δώσ' μου το, φέρ' το, πάρ' τα, άσ' το, γράψ' το**. In the same way σου, με and σε shorten before a vowel or another pronoun: **σ' αγαπώ, μ' αρέσει, σ' το είπα** (also written στο είπα).

blocks.title: Clitic doubling: topic and focus
blocks.text:
Greek can mention an object twice, once as a noun and once as a weak pronoun. This is not redundant: it marks the object as the **topic**, something already under discussion.

**Τον Γιάννη τον ξέρω.** 'John, I know (him).' The object is fronted and doubled: John is the topic, and what is new is that I know him.

**Τον Γιάννη ξέρω, όχι τον Νίκο.** No doubling: the fronted object is the **focus**, said with heavy stress: 'it's JOHN I know'.

**Τον ξέρω τον Γιάννη.** The object is added after the verb as an afterthought or a reminder of who you mean; very common in speech.

Doubling is the rule with fronted definite objects, with strong pronouns used for contrast (**Εμένα με ρώτησε**, **Εμένα μου αρέσει**), and with όλα: **Τα ξέρω όλα**. Indirect objects double too: **Στη Μαρία της το είπα**. Indefinite objects are normally not doubled: **Ένα βιβλίο διάβασα** is a focus statement, and *Ένα βιβλίο το διάβασα sounds wrong in most contexts.

blocks.text:
**Common mistakes.**

• Putting the pronoun after a να-verb: **Θέλω να το δω**, not *Θέλω να δω το.

• Putting it after a negative command: **Μην το πεις!**, not *Μην πες το.

• Accusative before genitive: **Μου το έδωσε**, not *Το μου έδωσε.

• Combining a 1st/2nd-person accusative with another pronoun: *Μου σε σύστησε is impossible; say **Σε σύστησε σε μένα** or **Με σύστησε σ' εσένα**.

• Copying English with λείπω and αρέσω: 'I miss you' = **Μου λείπεις**; 'she likes me' = **Της αρέσω**.

• Wrong case: **Με ρώτησε**, **Με βοήθησε** (acc.), but **Μου τηλεφώνησε**, **Μου είπε** (gen.).

• **Πάρε με τηλέφωνο** 'call me' vs **Πάρε μου ένα δώρο** 'buy me a present'.

• τες before the verb: **τις** βλέπω, never *τες βλέπω.

blocks.title: Τα κατάφερα: the τα that means nothing
blocks.text: Greek uses an empty neuter plural **τα** in dozens of idioms where nothing in particular is meant: **τα κατάφερα** 'I managed', **τα έχω χαμένα** 'I'm at a loss', **τα φτιάξανε** 'they got together (as a couple)', **τα χαλάσανε** 'they fell out, split up', **τα βρήκαμε** 'we came to an agreement', **τα λέμε** 'see you', **τα 'χει με τον Νίκο** 'she's going out with Nikos', and **Άσ' τα!** 'don't ask!'. Learn them as fixed chunks: the τα can never be left out, and it follows the normal rules for weak pronouns: **Δεν θα τα καταφέρω**, **Τα 'χουμε βρει**.

blocks.title: Το δώρο της μαμάς
blocks.en:
Eleni and her brother Kostas wanted to give their mother a present for her birthday. On Friday Eleni phoned him.

'Kostas, have you bought Mum's present?'

'Not yet. You told me you'd send me a photo of the necklace she likes, but you didn't send it to me.'

'I sent it to you last night! Didn't you see it? Look at your messages.'

'Oh yes, I see it now. It's nice. Where do they sell it?'

'In a shop on Ermou Street. Go tomorrow and get it. If they don't have it, ask the saleswoman whether she can order it.'

'OK. And who's going to give it to her?'

'We'll give it to her together, on Sunday, at lunch. Don't tell her anything until then!'

'I won't tell her, don't worry. But you know Mum: she notices everything. She'll ask me where I was on Saturday.'

'Tell her a friend called you and you went out for coffee.'

On Sunday their mother opened the box and looked at them, moved.

'My children, where did you find it? How did you know I liked it?'

'A little bird told us,' Eleni answered, and gave her a kiss.

items.prompt: Replace both objects with weak pronouns: Δίνω **το βιβλίο** **στη Μαρία**.
items.why: Genitive before accusative, both before the finite verb.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Θα στείλω **τα γράμματα** **στους γονείς μου**.
items.why: θα + gen + acc + verb: θα τους τα στείλω.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Έδειξα **τη φωτογραφία** **στον Νίκο**.
items.why: του + την (ν kept before a vowel) + verb.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Δεν είπα **την αλήθεια** **στη μητέρα μου**.
items.why: δεν + gen + acc + verb.

items.prompt: Replace both objects (use μου): Πρέπει να φέρεις **τα κλειδιά** **σε μένα**.
items.why: να + gen + acc + verb; nothing goes after the να-verb.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Μην πεις **το μυστικό** **στον Κώστα**!
items.why: A negative command is μη + dependent, so the pronouns go before the verb.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Έχω δει **την ταινία**.
items.why: In the perfect the pronoun precedes the auxiliary έχω.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Φέρε μου **το κλειδί**.
items.why: Imperative + two pronouns: gen + acc after the verb; φέρε μου το takes a second accent (or say φέρ' μου το).

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Δώσε **στον Γιάννη** **τα χρήματα**.
items.why: After an imperative: δώσ' του τα (or δώσε τού τα, δώσ' τα του).

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Πες **στη Μαρία** **το νέο**.
items.why: Imperative + gen + acc; the order after an imperative is flexible.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Στείλε μας **το αρχείο**.
items.why: Second-from-last stress + two pronouns: accent on the first pronoun (or στείλ' μας το).

items.prompt: Use a weak pronoun: Κοίταξε **εμένα**!
items.why: Stress on the third syllable from the end + pronoun: a second accent on -ξέ.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Διάβασε **το γράμμα**!
items.why: διάβασε + το: second accent on -σέ.

items.prompt: Replace both objects (use μου): Διάβασε **σε μένα** **το γράμμα**!
items.why: Three-syllable imperative + two pronouns: extra accent on the imperative.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Δίνοντας **στον Νίκο** **το κλειδί**…
items.why: Gerund: pronouns follow, with a second accent on the gerund.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Ας ρωτήσουμε **τον καθηγητή**.
items.why: ας + pronoun + verb.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Θα πάρω **τη Μαρία** τηλέφωνο.
items.why: παίρνω τηλέφωνο takes an accusative: την.

items.prompt: Replace the object: Θα τηλεφωνήσω **στη Μαρία**.
items.why: τηλεφωνώ σε + acc. becomes a genitive pronoun: της.

items.prompt: Τον Γιάννη ___ ξέρω από παιδί.
items.why: A fronted definite object (the topic) is doubled by a weak pronoun.

items.prompt: Το βιβλίο ___ διάβασα σε δύο μέρες.
items.why: Fronted topic object → doubling pronoun το.

items.prompt: Τις φωτογραφίες ___ έστειλα χθες.
items.why: Feminine plural before the verb is always τις.

items.prompt: Στη Μαρία ___ το είπα πρώτη.
items.why: Indirect objects double too: στη Μαρία… της.

items.prompt: Εμένα δεν ___ ρώτησε κανείς.
items.why: Strong pronoun for contrast + weak doubling; ρωτάω takes the accusative.

items.prompt: Εμένα ___ αρέσει το κρασί, όχι η μπίρα.
items.why: αρέσει takes a genitive experiencer.

items.prompt: Τα ξέρω ___. (all of them)
items.why: όλα doubles with τα: τα ξέρω όλα.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: I miss you. (εσύ)
items.why: The missed person is the subject of λείπω; the one who misses is genitive.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: Do you miss me?
items.why: Subject = me (λείπω), experiencer = you (σου).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: She likes me.
items.why: Subject = me (αρέσω), experiencer = her (της).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: I like you. (εσείς)
items.why: αρέσω agrees with the person liked: εσείς → αρέσετε.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: I don't mind.
items.why: πειράζει takes an accusative experiencer.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: I don't care.
items.why: νοιάζει takes the accusative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: My head hurts.
items.why: πονάει: the body part is the subject, the person accusative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: It's none of your business. (εσύ)
items.why: αφορά takes the accusative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: He asked me.
items.why: ρωτάω takes an accusative object, unlike English 'ask (to) me'.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: He phoned me. (τηλεφωνώ)
items.why: τηλεφωνώ σε → genitive pronoun; with παίρνω τηλέφωνο it is accusative: με πήρε.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: What's wrong with you? (εσύ)
items.why: συμβαίνει + genitive: 'what is happening to you'.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: That colour suits you. (εσύ)
accept: Σου πάει πολύ αυτό το χρώμα
items.why: πάει 'suits' + genitive.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: You deserve it. (εσύ)
items.why: αξίζει + genitive.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: Does the noise bother you? (εσύ, ενοχλώ)
items.why: ενοχλεί takes the accusative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: He owes me money.
items.why: χρωστάω: the creditor is genitive.

items.prompt: I want to see it.
items.why: After να the pronoun goes before the verb.

items.prompt: Don't tell him!
items.why: Negative commands use μη + dependent: pronouns before the verb.

items.prompt: I have seen it.
items.why: The pronoun precedes the auxiliary έχω.

items.prompt: Give it to me!
items.why: Positive imperative: pronouns follow, genitive μου for 'to me'.

items.prompt: I've already told you.
items.why: Nothing may come between the pronouns and the verb.

items.prompt: Looking at her, I understood.
items.why: Gerund + pronoun after it, accusative, with a second accent.

items.prompt: He introduced me to you.
items.why: Only 3rd-person accusatives combine with a genitive pronoun.

items.prompt: It's JOHN I know, not Nick.
items.answer: Τον Γιάννη ξέρω, όχι τον Νίκο.
options: Τον Γιάννη ξέρω, όχι τον Νίκο.
Τον Γιάννη τον ξέρω, όχι τον Νίκο.
Τον ξέρω τον Γιάννη, όχι τον Νίκο.
items.why: A fronted object without doubling is the focus.

items.prompt: He helped me.
items.why: βοηθάω takes a direct (accusative) object.

items.prompt: Call me tomorrow!
items.why: παίρνω τηλέφωνο + accusative; the pronoun follows the imperative.

items.prompt: I like them (the shoes).
items.why: The liked things are the subject: plural αρέσουν.

items.prompt: Read it to me!
items.why: Extra accent on the imperative before two pronouns. Μου το διάβασε means 'he read it to me'.

items.prompt: Ένα βιβλίο ___ διάβασα όλο το καλοκαίρι.
items.why: Indefinite fronted objects are focus and are not doubled.
